body.statement: Theorem 2 (SparseSIM-ID completeness). For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), under Theorem 1, \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminates after at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) exact rational-table checks and returns exactly one of two mutually exclusive certificates: either one observable arithmetic circuit \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\) with identities proving \(T_{D,y}=T_{D_0,y}\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) for every \(D,y\), or \((D_0,D,p^{\dagger})\) with \(p^{\dagger}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and \((T_{D,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\ne(T_{D_0,y}(p^{\dagger}))_y\). The first branch occurs if and only if the intervention law is common to every represented DAG. On tied SA-MPDAG families this is a strict decision-theoretic tightening of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo: every query passing their sufficient graphical test is on the equality branch, while every query failing that test is still decided by an equality certificate or a rational positive separator. When \(\mathfrak G\) is a singleton and \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) equals its full positive Markov model, the decision agrees with Perkovic's single-MPDAG criterion and generalized truncated factorization.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted \(\mathfrak u\).  First suppose that every normal form is zero.  The finite identities supplied by the narrowed certificate lemma have, for each \((D,y)\), the form
\[
 s^{N_{D,y}}\left(F_{D,y}^{2k_{D,y}}+
       \sum_iq_{D,y,i}^2\right)=\sum_j a_{D,y,j}f_j,
 \qquad J_{\mathcal I}=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\rangle .
\]
Let \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  The oracle-one and normalization conditions in \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\) give \(f_j(p)=0\) for every \(j\).  Strict positivity gives \(p_z>0\).  Every recorded denominator is a product of observed marginal probabilities, each of which is a nonempty sum of positive cells; hence \(B_{D,y}(p)>0\) for every \((D,y)\), and therefore \(s(p)\neq0\).  Evaluating the certificate and dividing by \(s(p)^{N_{D,y}}\) yields
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)^{2k_{D,y}}+\sum_iq_{D,y,i}(p)^2=0.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative, so \(F_{D,y}(p)=0\).  By the cross-signature definition and positivity of both denominators,
\[
 0=A_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)-A_{D_0,y}(p)B_{D,y}(p)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p).
\]
This holds for every \(D,y,p\), proving soundness of the equality circuit and its common-law conclusion.

For the second branch, an integer of bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) has fewer than \(2^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1}\) signed possibilities.  A reduced rational coordinate therefore has fewer than \(2^{2(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) numerator--denominator descriptions.  Taking \(m\) coordinates gives fewer than
\[
 2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
descriptions, before positivity, normalization, or coprimality removes any of them.  Canonical finite enumeration consequently checks no more than this number of distinct candidates.  Exact checks of positivity, normalization, oracle-one equations, every oracle-zero sum of squares, and a failed signature decide whether a candidate belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and separates.  The enumeration returns if and only if at least one such bounded candidate exists.  For a returned candidate \(p^\dagger\), denominator positivity and \(F_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq0\) give
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger),
\]
so the two intervention vectors differ.  This is incompatible with the universal equality certified by the first branch, establishing mutual exclusivity and soundness.  The argument supplies no bounded rational candidate merely from a nonzero normal form, which is why no unconditional termination claim is made.
body.justification: The theorem replaces arbitrary selection among tied sparsest graphs by an effect-complete common-functional-or-counterexample contract.
body.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo prove only a sufficient simultaneous criterion; Perkovic is complete for one MPDAG rather than a tied family across MECs.
body.consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP all-ties output can report a common effect circuit or an exact ambiguity table instead of choosing one tied graph.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove that every nonzero-normal-form branch contains a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator within the declared finite height bound.
obligation.obstruction: The branch termination claim is exactly the unresolved forward implication of the rational-positive separation theorem; a nonzero real-radical remainder alone does not ensure a bounded rational separator in the required sign chamber.
obligation.attempted: Equality-branch soundness, exact candidate checking, the search-cardinality bound, and soundness of every returned separator are established separately. These arguments do not force a qualifying table for an arbitrary nonzero branch, because saturation does not select the positive exact-oracle chamber and supplies no rational-point height bound.
obligation.partial_result:
The equality output and every returned separator are sound by \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}bounded\text{-}search\text{-}certificate\text{-}soundness}\). The latter also proves that the prescribed rational search has at most
\[
2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
candidate descriptions. Each candidate is checked exactly for positivity, normalization, all bit-one equalities, all bit-zero inequalities, and a failed cross-signature. Hence, conditional on the existence of a separating table of coordinate bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the nonzero-normal-form branch terminates within the displayed bound and returns two represented DAGs with distinct intervention vectors. What is not established is that every nonzero-normal-form branch contains such a bounded rational table; exhaustion of the finite list therefore need not produce either advertised certificate under the frozen hypotheses alone.
